title: Frontend OpenFeature hooks/typings are typed from the flag's Expression, not just boolean
answers: How do I add a non-boolean feature flag (number/string/object) with a typed React hook?
Why is my flag's generated useFlag hook typed as boolean when its value is a string/number/object?
How does the generator decide the TS type of a feature flag's React hook?
body: Root cause: generateOpenFeatureReactForFlags used to hardcode Type: "boolean" for every flag regardless of its Expression value. Fix pattern: parse the flag's Expression with setting.ParseFlag, derive its FlagType via TypedFlag(...).GetFlagType(), and map FlagTypeBoolean/Integer/Float/String/Object to "boolean"/"number"/"number"/"string"/"object" respectively (pkg/services/featuremgmt/toggles_gen_test.go:getOpenFeatureReactFlag). This same mapping feeds both the generated hook (useFlag<Type>) and the TS key unions (BooleanFlagKey/NumberFlagKey/StringFlagKey/ObjectFlagKey) in generateOpenFeatureReactTypingsForFlags — they must stay in sync since both derive from the same per-flag Type. Constraints: applies to any flag with Generate.React: true; a flag whose Expression doesn't parse into one of the five known FlagTypes causes getOpenFeatureReactFlag to t.Fatalf, so new flag value shapes must be added to setting.ParseFlag/TypedFlag first.
applies: Frontend feature-flag registry entries generated into React OpenFeature hooks/typings (standardFeatureFlags with Generate.React: true).

The same Type mapping feeds both the generated hook (useFlag<Type>) and TS key unions (BooleanFlagKey/NumberFlagKey/StringFlagKey/ObjectFlagKey)—both must stay in sync. Applies only to standardFeatureFlags with Generate.React: true; a flag whose Expression doesn't parse into one of the five known FlagTypes causes t.Fatalf, requiring new value shapes to be added to setting.ParseFlag/TypedFlag first. Paths: pkg/services/featuremgmt/toggles_gen_test.go:getOpenFeatureReactFlag, generateOpenFeatureReactTypingsForFlags.
